speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of the right flank pain and how long you have been experiencing the hematuria?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain radiate to your groin or lower abdomen, and have you experienced any nausea or vomiting alongside it? Also, do you have a history of kidney stones or gout?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a fever or chills, and is the pain constant or does it come in waves? I would also like to know if you have any difficulty or burning sensation when urinating.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify if you are currently experiencing fever, chills, or nausea, as these signs would point toward an infection or obstruction. Additionally, does the pain come in waves and radiate to the groin, or is it a constant dull ache? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recurrent UTIs, hematuria, and flank pain without fever or dysuria, I suspect a structural abnormality or stone. REQUEST TEST: Non-contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the non-contrast CT was normal, I need to evaluate for vascular causes or soft tissue abnormalities that CT might miss. REQUEST TEST: Renal Ultrasound with Doppler

speaker: Doctor
text: Since imaging and urinalysis are non-diagnostic for stones or acute infection, I must consider renal cell carcinoma or other malignancies. REQUEST TEST: CT Urogram with contrast

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal imaging and persistent sterile pyuria, I suspect tuberculosis of the urinary tract. REQUEST TEST: Urine Culture and Urine AFB Smear
